title: Sharpen Your Creative Thinking With Random Words
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article revives the largely forgotten creativity exercises of psychologist Edward de Bono, who believed creativity was a trainable skill rather than an innate gift. It describes three of his random-word exercises: using one random word to define a problem and another to suggest a solution; describing how five random words might influence one another; and chaining connections between successive random words. The piece frames these lateral-thinking drills as a kind of mental gym and notes their modern echo in the popularity of word-based games, closing with an invitation to use a smartphone-generated word list to start practicing.
points: Edward de Bono, author of more than 80 books, believed creativity is a skill that can be trained like any other.
His Random Words List, once popular, is largely forgotten but easy to recreate with a smartphone.
One exercise: use one random word to name a problem, then find a solution among four other random words.
A second exercise asks how five random words might influence each other.
A third exercise chains connections between successively drawn random words.
quotes: No one has thought more about creativity in a lifetime than famed psychologist and physician Edward de Bono.
He believed creativity is a skill that can be learned, developed, and applied.
De Bono relied upon random words to teach creativity and designed exercises that trained the creative mind.
De Bono designed dozens of similar exercises that formed a mental gym for developing creative thinking habits and skills.
Words are full of possibility, and possibility is the key to creativity.
